original_value: Since the first publications related to microstructured optical fibers (MOFs), the development of optical fiber sensors (OFS) based on them has attracted the interest of many research groups because of the market niches that can take advantage of their specific features. Due to their unique structure based on a certain distribution of air holes, MOFs are especially useful for sensing applications: on one hand, the increased coupling of guided modes into the cladding or the holes enhances significantly the interaction with sensing films deposited there; on the other hand, MOF air holes enhance the direct interaction between the light and the analytes that get into in these cavities. Consequently, the sensitivity when detecting liquids, gasses or volatile organic compounds (VOCs) is significantly improved. This paper is focused on the reported sensors that have been developed with MOFs which are applied to detection of gases and VOCs, highlighting the advantages that this type of fiber offers.

result.paraphrase: Since the earliest publications on microstructured optical fibers (MOFs), many research groups have been interested in developing optical fiber sensors (OFS) based on them because they can fill market niches that benefit from their distinctive characteristics. Owing to their unique arrangement of air holes, MOFs are particularly well suited to sensing applications: first, stronger coupling of guided modes into the cladding or the holes greatly improves interaction with sensing films deposited there; second, the air holes in MOFs increase direct interaction between the light and analytes entering these cavities. As a result, sensitivity for detecting liquids, gases, or volatile organic compounds (VOCs) is significantly enhanced. This paper concentrates on reported MOF-based sensors for gas and VOC detection, emphasizing the advantages offered by this type of fiber.
